extracted.intended_audience: researchers, program designers, policymakers, and industry/community partners involved in CIHR's Environments and Health Signature Initiative (Alberta)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and implementing Environments and Health Signature Initiative (EHSI) research projects and partnerships in Alberta, focusing on stakeholder engagement, transdisciplinary collaboration, knowledge translation, and policy impact. Aimed at aligning research priorities with industry, community and government needs to deliver usable solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry engagement is critical
rubrics_metrics.description: For this research initiative to resonate in Alberta, industry engagement is critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage industry so they see advantage in participating; include the resource sector and work through sector associations to build in‑roads. Consider 'unusual' industry partners (e.g., insurance) and ensure industry has a voice in planning so their views are incorporated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on provincial priorities and research gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the priorities that are most important for the province and focus on the research gaps that currently exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize a broad prevention focus on environments and health to identify correct priorities; align research topics with industry's research priorities where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear value proposition for industry
rubrics_metrics.description: The initiative must present a strong value proposition that has appeal for industry and their issues (e.g., social license to operate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design projects so industry can see advantages to being at the table; use short-term wins when necessary to secure buy-in but ensure overall value is compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nexus approach focused on tangible solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The EHSI 'nexus' approach differs from CIHR open investigator‑driven programs by tackling big problems and seeking to deliver relevant, tangible solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers must understand this fundamental difference; project design should prioritize problem-driven, solution-oriented work rather than purely investigator-led curiosity research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge translation (KT) deeply embedded
rubrics_metrics.description: It's imperative that KT is deeply embedded in EHSI projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate resources to KT, value KT in performance measurement, and ensure results are translated into usable formats rather than sitting unused. Plan for ongoing KT activities as part of project budgets and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable trans-disciplinary teams and bridging roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Build an enabling environment for large trans-disciplinary teams and include people who can bridge systems as well as specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine boundary-spanning personnel with domain experts to facilitate collaboration across disciplines and sectors; provide supports that allow such large teams to function effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner fit: right people on right projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Success is predicated on the right people partnering together on the right projects; finding this 'fit' takes time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time in partner identification and relationship-building; assess partnerships for complementary goals and capabilities before committing to projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-sector collaborations aligning interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations need to allow community, academic, government and industry interests to be met, and historically industry has often been left out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agree on real-world issues to address and find ways to align differing incentives across sectors to enable meaningful collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve knowledge users in research design
rubrics_metrics.description: It's vital that knowledge users be involved in the research design to promote buy-in and demonstrate the value of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage communities and other end users early so projects help solve community problems and communities assist in identifying the issues they want resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research must lead to policy-relevant action
rubrics_metrics.description: Research from this initiative must result in significant follow-through that shapes public policy development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create stronger links between 'what we know' (research findings) and 'what we do' (policy shifts). Design projects with pathways to influence policy and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collapse silos via cross-sector problem solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex problems demand cross-sectoral problem solving; there is an opportunity to collapse silos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote partnership-based research that provides mutual benefit to researchers and policy makers and enables proactive, integrated responses to complex issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate research for public consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Research has to be translated into something usable and consumable for the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for early and ongoing public engagement using a range of tools, and be willing to interpret and explain findings so they are accessible and actionable by the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to long-term funding and patience
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the desire for 'quick wins'—complex problems require commitment over time, sustained funding, and willingness to look beyond budget and political cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While short-term projects may help secure industry buy-in, design the initiative with long-term funding horizons and expectations for sustained engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate partner input into design and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR is committed to ensuring partner input is addressed in the design and implementation of the Environments and Health Signature Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stakeholder consultations (industry, government, community partners) to shape program features, eligibility, and priorities so the initiative is meaningful and relevant to regional needs.
